what: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: modelterms lightweight, zero-dependency R package providing unified interface manipulating stats::terms objects, formulas, fitted models, character vectors term labels. designed standalone utility statistical modeling workflows core infrastructure module packages (including midr).

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: R, model terms serve structural blueprint predictive models—role paramount importance additive models built stats::lm(), stats::glm(), GAMs. However, word “terms” historically suffered ambiguity R. instance, terms argument stats::predict.lm() expects character vector term labels, whereas "terms" object stored inside fitted model formula-like object packed complex attributes. Despite representing structural concepts, directly interchangeable. Furthermore, Base R’s stats::terms() stats::drop.terms() provide powerful formula parsing, working programmatically often involves sharp edges: Inconsistent Coercion: stats::terms() directly coerce character vector term labels like c("x1", "x2"), stats::reformulate(character(0)) throws error. Unwanted Reordering & Renaming: Even keep.order = TRUE, stats::terms() silently rewrites interaction labels based variable appearance order (e.g., turning c("", "b:") c("", ":b")). Fragile Subsetting: stats::drop.terms() requires numeric indices, loses response variable default, crashes predictor terms dropped. Ambiguous “Variables”: Base R lacks unified API distinguish term labels (additive components, e.g., "x1:log(x2)"), model variables (transformed expressions formula, e.g., "log(x2)"), underlying raw variables (column names data.frame, e.g., "x2"). modelterms resolves issues clean, pipe-friendly functional API.

what: Core Concepts: Three Levels of Model Components
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: Consider formula y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + (x1 * x2). modelterms clearly distinguishes three structural levels: Setting .term = TRUE get_variables() returns named list mapping term label constituent variables:
code: library(modelterms)  fml_demo <- y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2) get_variables(fml_demo, raw = TRUE, by.term = TRUE) #> $x1 #> [1] "x1" #>  #> $`log(x2)` #> [1] "x2" #>  #> $`I(x1 * x2)` #> [1] "x1" "x2" #>  #> $`x1:log(x2)` #> [1] "x1" "x2"

what: 1. Flexible and Safe Coercion with as_terms()
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: as_terms() seamlessly converts terms objects, formulas, fitted models (lm, glm, etc.), character vectors valid stats::terms object, allowing --fly modification response variable intercept. Strict Term Label Vectors (length >= 2): Every element must valid single term. Input order exact interaction notation ("b:") strictly preserved. Formula Shorthand (length == 1): single string containing formula operators (e.g., ".^2" "* b + c") expanded right-hand side formula expression.
code: # Preserves exact order and "b:a" notation for term label vectors t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1")) get_labels(t1) #> [1] "b:a" "a" has_intercept(t1) #> [1] TRUE  # Expands length-1 formula shorthands (including "." with data) t2 <- as_terms(".^2", response = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4]) get_labels(t2) #> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp" #> [6] "Wind:Temp"

what: 2. Subsetting, Filtering, and Modifying Terms with filter_terms()
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: filter_terms() declarative, crash-safe replacement stats::drop.terms(), stats::delete.response(), [.terms. can subset terms directly label index, filter interaction order constituent variables, modify response intercept—even predictor terms filtered .
code: fml <- log(Ozone) ~ Solar.R + Wind + Temp + Wind:Temp + Solar.R:Wind  # Extract main effects only fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels() #> [1] "Solar.R" "Wind"    "Temp"  # Keep terms involving "Wind", but exclude any term involving "Solar.R" sub_terms <- filter_terms(fml, require = "Wind", remove = "Solar.R") get_labels(sub_terms) #> [1] "Wind"      "Wind:Temp"  # Drop specific interactions (order-invariantly) and replace the response variable filter_terms(fml, drop = "Temp:Wind", response = "Ozone") #> Ozone ~ 1 + Solar.R + Wind + Temp + Solar.R:Wind #> attr(,"variables") #> list(Ozone, Solar.R, Wind, Temp) #> attr(,"factors") #>         Solar.R Wind Temp Solar.R:Wind #> Ozone         0    0    0            0 #> Solar.R       1    0    0            1 #> Wind          0    1    0            1 #> Temp          0    0    1            0 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 1 1 1 2 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: R_GlobalEnv>  # Directly use the filtered terms object to fit a submodel lm_sub <- lm(sub_terms, data = airquality) coef(lm_sub) #>  (Intercept)         Wind    Wind:Temp  #>  4.187217000 -0.410375120  0.004366689

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: users specify interaction terms plotting evaluation functions, may write "Temp:Wind" instead "Wind:Temp". match_labels() normalizes matches terms regardless variable order safely handling multi-term expressions like "Wind * Temp".
code: labs <- c("x1", "log(x2)", "x1:log(x2)", "I(1:100):x1")  # Matches reversed interaction notation to the canonical model labels match_labels(c("log(x2):x1", "x1:I(1:100)", "x1"), labs) #>    log(x2):x1   x1:I(1:100)            x1  #>  "x1:log(x2)" "I(1:100):x1"          "x1"  # Safely handles unmatched or invalid expressions ("omit", "pass", or "fail") match_labels(c("x1", "x1 * x2", "unknown"), labs, nomatch = "pass") #>      x1 x1 * x2 unknown  #>    "x1"      NA      NA

text: x, y object representing model terms: terms object, formula, fitted model object, character vector. match_labels(), y target object whose term labels matched . response optional response specification as_terms() filter_terms(). NULL (default) TRUE, retains existing response x (response x character vector). FALSE, removes response variable. character string language object, sets replaces response variable. intercept optional logical as_terms() filter_terms(). NULL (default), retains existing intercept status x (defaults intercept character vectors unless explicit tokens like "1" "+1" present x). TRUE FALSE, explicitly forces removes intercept. data data.frame used resolve . formulas shorthand strings. keep.order logical. terms kept input order rather sorted interaction order? Defaults TRUE strict term label vectors FALSE formulas length-1 formula shorthands. env environment attach resulting terms object coercing character vector. Defaults parent.frame(). ... additional arguments passed terms as_terms(). keep, drop character vector term labels (matched order-invariantly via match_labels()) integer vector term indices explicitly retain (keep) exclude (drop) filter_terms(). order integer vector specifying interaction orders retain filter_terms() (e.g., 1L main effects, 2L two-way interactions). require character vector variable names. terms containing least one variables retained. remove character vector variable names. terms containing variables excluded. raw logical. title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: model formula y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + (x1 * x2), package distinguishes three structural levels: Term Labels (get_labels(x)):     individual additive components model:     c("x1", "log(x2)", "x1:log(x2)", "(x1 * x2)"). Model Variables (get_variables(x, raw = FALSE)):     distinct predictor expressions forming terms (rows "factors" matrix):     c("x1", "log(x2)", "(x1 * x2)"). Raw Variables (get_variables(x, raw = TRUE)):     underlying column names required data:     c("x1", "x2").

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: x character vector, as_terms() distinguishes vector strict term labels length-1 formula shorthand: Strict Term Labels (character(n)): every element (excluding     intercept tokens like "1" "-1") represents strictly single valid     term (e.g., c("b:", "", "(x^2)")), input order exact interaction notation     ("b:") preserved default (keep.order = TRUE). Length-1 Formula Shorthand (character(1)): x single     string containing formula operators . (e.g., ".^2", ".",     "* b + c + 1"), expanded right-hand side formula expression     (using data needed) sorted interaction order default     (keep.order = FALSE). Invalid Mixed Vectors (length(x) >= 2): x length 2     contains non-single-term expression (c("* b", "c")     c(".", "")), informative error thrown.

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: filter_terms() serves declarative, crash-safe replacement drop.terms, delete.response, [.terms: Direct Subsetting: Pass character labels integer indices keep     (second argument) drop extract exclude specific terms (order-invariantly)     preserving intercept response. Structural Filtering: Use order, require, remove     filter terms interaction order constituent variables. Response & Intercept Control: as_terms()     filter_terms(), set response = FALSE remove response variable     (like stats::delete.response(x)), pass new variable name replace , set     intercept = TRUE / FALSE without crashing even predictor terms dropped.

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
code: # Coercion with as_terms() t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1")) get_labels(t1) #> [1] "b:a" "a"   has_intercept(t1) #> [1] TRUE  t2 <- as_terms(".^2", response = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4]) get_labels(t2) #> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp" #> [6] "Wind:Temp"     # Extracting labels, variables, and response at three levels fml <- log(y) ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2) get_response(fml, raw = FALSE) #> [1] "log(y)" get_response(fml, raw = TRUE) #> [1] "y" get_labels(fml) #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" "x1:log(x2)" get_variables(fml, raw = FALSE) #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE) #> [1] "x1" "x2" get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE, by.term = TRUE) #> $x1 #> [1] "x1" #>  #> $`log(x2)` #> [1] "x2" #>  #> $`I(x1 * x2)` #> [1] "x1" "x2" #>  #> $`x1:log(x2)` #> [1] "x1" "x2" #>   # Subsetting, filtering, and modifying response/intercept fml |> filter_terms("log(x2):x1") #> log(y) ~ 1 + x1:log(x2) #> attr(,"variables") #> list(log(y), x1, log(x2)) #> attr(,"factors") #>         x1:log(x2) #> log(y)           0 #> x1               2 #> log(x2)          2 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "x1:log(x2)" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 2 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: 0x5c37e20165d0> fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels() #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" fml |> filter_terms(require = "x2", remove = "x1", raw = TRUE) |> get_labels() #> [1] "log(x2)" fml |> filter_terms(drop = "log(x2):x1", response = FALSE) #> ~1 + x1 + log(x2) + I(x1 * x2) #> attr(,"variables") #> list(x1, log(x2), I(x1 * x2)) #> attr(,"factors") #>            x1 log(x2) I(x1 * x2) #> x1          1       0          0 #> log(x2)     0       1          0 #> I(x1 * x2)  0       0          1 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 1 1 1 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 0 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: 0x5c37e20165d0> fml |> filter_terms(order = 1, response = "yhat", intercept = FALSE) #> yhat ~ -1 + x1 + log(x2) + I(x1 * x2) #> attr(,"variables") #> list(yhat, x1, log(x2), I(x1 * x2)) #> attr(,"factors") #>            x1 log(x2) I(x1 * x2) #> yhat        0       0          0 #> x1          1       0          0 #> log(x2)     0       1          0 #> I(x1 * x2)  0       0          1 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 1 1 1 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 0 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: 0x5c37e20165d0>  # Order-invariant label matching match_labels(c("x1", "log(x2):x1", "I(x2 * x1)"), fml, nomatch = "pass") #>           x1   log(x2):x1   I(x2 * x1)  #>         "x1" "x1:log(x2)"           NA
